title: Stationary motocross drive effort across real traffic interruptions
status: Complete: four focused before/after production cases, exact isolated wet event and final original complete 20-jump / three-start / ten-event gate verified.

diagnosis.witness: Actual wet Valley Moto 2 rider 4 remains at station 315.399 m while passing traffic alternates drive and brake commands. Each brake intervention reset the original four-second effort clock without physical movement. The eventual normal five-second remount was functioning correctly.
diagnosis.instrumentation: Read-only observation of production Simulation.step followed by importing the unchanged original race script; no state, input or validator changes.

correction.pause: While riding, grounded and slower than 0.5 m/s, a tick without a drive request leaves accumulated drive effort unchanged.
correction.countAndTrigger: Only current target > 0.5 m/s, throttle > 0.2 and brake < 0.1 accrue dt and can request assistance after the original four seconds.
correction.reset: Actual motion at or above 0.5 m/s, flight, nonriding state or inactive/initial race resets effort.
correction.scope: DirtBikeAIDriver only. Shared BikeVehicle six-second fallback, normal five-second remount, player controls and all jump/landing/crash/stop thresholds are unchanged.

fixture.physics: Production Simulation, DirtBikeVehicle contact, AI and traffic planning. No private effort clock or fabricated AI pedals.
fixture.traffic: A real second rider is placed 2.8 m ahead for two seconds, then 40 m ahead for two seconds. This deliberately staged traffic fixture produces the pedal interruptions through the actual controller.
fixture.movementResetExplanation: The public body velocity receives a 2 m/s forward push at t=2 s; the bike physically moves. The last speed >=0.5 sample before assistance is t=2.3833 s and assistance begins t=6.4 s, a fresh 4.0167 seconds later.
fixture.manualRemountExplanation: A public restart at t=2 s enters the actual remount state. The bike returns to riding at t=6.9917 s, is placed back on the same beached face, and requires a fresh drive interval before assistance at t=11.125 s.
fixture.queueCaveat: The traffic controller receives its normal initial evaluation; assertions require sustained throttle <0.01 and brake >0.9 after the first second, no significant motion and no assistance through 14 seconds.

limits: Deterministic CPU witnesses, one exact event replay and a complete original ten-event gate; no claim covering every seed or real hardware.
Pit, traffic, local flags and deformed terrain couple race trajectories; the lower crash count does not prove that the clock correction directly prevents each crash.
The staged traffic fixture deliberately controls blocker location; it is distinct from the unmodified whole-race replay.
